idiom_name: BallItem/BallThread pair with a package-private twin field, wired by a static factory
implementation_notes: A Java class has exactly one superclass (JLS 8.1.4: 'Each class except Object is an extension of (that is, a subclass of) a single existing class'), so a ball that must be a GameItem and a Thread becomes two classes in one package, each extending one parent and each holding a reference to its twin; the field is package-private so the pair reaches into each other's state without publishing it - the pattern's data-abstraction consequence - and a static creation method such as GameItem.newBall builds and links both ends before returning one. What replaces the classic structure today: Java 8 default methods let an interface carry behaviour (but 'interfaces have no instance variables'), and virtual threads (Java 21) remove the specific 'must extend Thread' motivation because Runnable tasks are scheduled by the JVM; keep the twin when both parents are classes that own state and cannot be refactored.
pitfalls: The twin field must stay package-private (or be reached through a package-private setter): a public getter publishes the partner to every client and throws away the encapsulation concession the pattern already made.

Both ends keep each other strongly reachable for a cycle collector, but a long-lived Thread (or a framework registry holding the platform end) also keeps the abstraction end alive unless one link is cleared on teardown or held as a WeakReference.
The pair's invariant - both links set - is not expressible in the type system: a partially initialised BallItem is a NullPointerException waiting for the first click.
Concurrency is not part of the pattern: if the platform end runs the entity while the click path mutates the same state, the crossing flags must be volatile or both ends confined to one thread.

variants.name: Behaviour-only second protocol absorbed as default methods (Java 8+)
variants.idiom_name: abstraction end implements the crossing protocol as default methods; only the platform end stays a real object
variants.implementation_notes: Java 8 interfaces may carry default implementations - 'A default method is an instance method declared in an interface with the default modifier' (JLS 9) - so when the second hierarchy is behaviour without state, the twin end collapses into interface defaults and only the class carrying state remains a real object. The crossing calls still go to the platform end as plain delegation, and the interface may be implemented by delegation to the partner (a hand-written delegating method or an explicit inner implementation). Keep the classic pair whenever the second parent owns instance state: interfaces still have no instance variables, so state cannot be moved into the interface.
pitfalls: Default methods are reached through the interface type; calling toggle() on the class requires the class to declare an override.
Diamond rule: two superinterfaces providing the same default method must both be overridden by the implementing class or the class does not compile - keep capability interfaces disjoint.
Interfaces cannot hold instance state, so a second parent with fields still needs the classic two-class pair; static fields are not a substitute.
Default methods are inherited by every implementer, so adding one to a widely implemented interface changes behaviour silently for all of them unless the addition is deliberate.
